newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ATHLETICS-CARL LEWIS TO RUN IN AUSTRALIA AND NZ.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CARL LEWIS TO RUN IN AUSTRALIA AND NZ.

text.p: Nine-times Olympic gold medallist Carl Lewis will begin what is expected to be his last year in athletics by racing in New Zealand and Australia later this month, Australian athletics officials said on Wednesday.
Lewis, 35, will run his favourite 100 metres in grand prix events in Auckland on January 25 and in Sydney two days later, an Athletics Australia spokesman said.

"Carl has never raced in Australia before and we understand he is keen to go to those countries where he hasn't raced before and compete in front of crowds who haven't had the chance to see him," spokesman Damian Booth said.
He said Lewis had decided not to compete in the long jump, the event in which he won the last of his nine Olympic golds at last year's Atlanta Games.
"We understand that he will only do the 100 metres now, that he has pretty much given the long jump away," Booth said.
Lewis's Atlanta long jump gold came at the end of a stellar career encompassing four Olympic Games.
Lewis came from well behind in the Atlanta competition, summoning all his spirit to snatch gold with a final leap of 8.50 metres.

That effort followed his triumphs in the same event in Los Angeles in 1984, Seoul in 1988 and Barcelona in 1992 and made him the only athlete apart from American discus thrower Al Oerter to win the same athletics event at four Games.
Lewis also joined Finnish runner Paavo Nurmi, Soviet gymnast Larisa Latynina and American swimmer Mark Spitz as record winners of nine gold medals.
His five sprint medals came in the 100, 200 and 4x100 metres relay in Los Angeles, the 100 metres in Seoul and the 4x100 relay in Barcelona.
